svg.title: v11 MLA decode kernel schedule on B300/sm_103 (nsys 2025.3.2): one fused split-KV partial kernel owns 99.9% of GPU time, the LSE merge and torch quant/page setup are negligible — so the bottleneck is INSIDE the partial kernel (per-CTA), not the launch/merge structure
svg.desc: An nsys GPU-kernel-time breakdown for the v11 MLA latent-KV decode at N_k=1,048,576 on a B300/sm_103, captured with nsys 2025.3.2 (which produced a non-empty sm_103 trace, paying v10's provenance debt). A single horizontal proportion bar shows mla_partial_kernel, templated <TN=32, DQK=576, DV=512>, taking 99.9% of GPU time: 100 instances, total 38,708,710,496 ns, averaging 387.087 ms per launch. Everything else is a hairline sliver: the LSE mla_merge_kernel is 100 calls at 3,499.5 ns each, total 349,953 ns, which is 0.0009% of GPU time (nsys prints this as 0.0%; the docs' "0.04%" label was a 44x overstatement). Torch one-time setup — NVFP4 quantization, abs/amax, searchsorted page-table build, radix sort — together is under 0.01%. Reconciliation: 387 ms/call at N_k=1M corresponds to the regime bench's 3023 us/tok x 128 heads (a 0.03% match). The schedule itself is HEALTHY (one fused partial kernel, a trivial merge, no launch-bound or merge-bound pathology), so the measured ~4x-slower-than-torch and 0.75 TFLOP/s ceiling (under 1% of either compute peak, %HBM ~0%) live INSIDE the partial kernel — a per-CTA / low-MLP limit (warp-per-head CUDA-core GEMV at N_q=1), not a structural one. This stays fixed from v3's 88.6%-pass2-wall problem. Owed: ncu L2-hit-rate (the unprivileged container blocks counters).
svg.text: GPU time by kernel (nsys cuda_gpu_kern_sum) — N_k=1,048,576
Time is all in the fused partial kernel; the wall is inside it (per-CTA), not the merge.
